newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki misses rally, ends about flat for Easter.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki misses rally, ends about flat for Easter.

text.p: Shares failed to join a broad European rally on Wednesday after an expected U.S. rate hike as dividend payments weighed on several shares, brokers said.

However, sentiment improved as markets shrugged off the U.S. tightening, volume became healthier at 620 million markka, and the HEX yield index which ignores the impact of dividends rose 0.52 percent.

The HEX general index edged just into positive territory after a weak start and closed 0.1 percent up at 2,847.78 points, 0.3 percent above last Friday's close. The market closed for Easter and next trading day is Tuesday.
"The market now has room to recover because the rate decision is out of the way," one broker said. "There's been latent buying interest after recent declines," said another.
Telecoms major Nokia fell 2.50 markka to close at 298.50, after going ex a 3.50 markka dividend.

Pharmaceuticals group Orion extended recent gains in lively volume on foreign buying interest following news it had successfully tested a drug that enhances the effects of conventional Parkinson's disease drugs.
It closed up 8.00 markka or over four percent at 195.00.
"Orion has definitely been the most interesting share of the day," one broker said.
The financial sector outperformed led by insurer Sampo's 3.15 percent gain to 459.00 markka.
Plastics pipes and furniture group Asko was the most traded share, falling only 5.00 markka to 445.00 though it went ex a 10 markka dividend.
